papers.title: Ancestral and derived feeding morphology during rapid ecological divergence within a species
papers.abstract: Derived characters that may have emerged via positive selection can be identified by comparing species, but also possibly subgroups within species. Allopatric and sympatric polymorphism observed in many salmonids is thought to emerge mainly in landlocked populations, which have lost the anadromous lifestyle of their ancestors. Populations of Arctic charr (Salvelinus alpinus) are an example of such polymorphism, commonly diverging along a pelagic-benthic axis. Populations of Icelandic charr can be anadromous or landlocked, like in Lake Thingvallavatn where four morphs coexist differing in habitat use, preferred prey and external feeding morphology. Three of these morphs are also caught in the neighboring Lake Ulfljotsvatn, despite prey availability in the two lakes differing notably. We studied variation of craniofacial morphology in Icelandic charr populations and compared the ecologically specialized sympatric morphs to five anadromous charr populations and to two non-specialized lake populations, as well as across two connected lakes. The results indicate minor variation among anadromous populations and that the benthic lake forms are derived. There was clear phenotypic difference between benthic and pelagic morphs within Thingvallavatn but no differences between the morphs in Ulfljotsvatn. Patterns of variation between corresponding morphs across the two lakes suggest genetics separation and phenotypic plasticity.

papers.title: Monolayer, Spheroid, and Organoid Formats Elicit Proteomic States that Couple Organelle Organization to Metabolic Vulnerabilities
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) cell culture systems are becoming more widely applied to model tissue organization, disease progression, and therapeutic response. Yet, the molecular characteristics that distinguish organoids and spheroids from conventional monolayer culture are incompletely defined. Here, using tumorigenic organoid models of high-grade serous tubo-ovarian cancer (HGSC), we establish a quantitative proteomic resource that reveals how cell architecture and media independently but jointly shape the cellular state in organoids, spheroids, and monolayers. We further pursue HGSC subtype-enriched features within this framework and identify that a poor prognosis-associated genotype with reported paclitaxel hypersensitivity, Trp53-/-;Pten-/-;Nf1-/- (PPN), is marked by increased microtubule-associated proteins, lipid-associated factors, and mitochondrial remodeling. PPN cells displayed clustered lipid droplets, whereby mitochondria-ER tethering increased. Relative to Trp53-/- (P) and a frequent HGSC genotype, Trp53-/-;Brca1+/-;MycOE (PBM), live-cell imaging showed that PPN exhibits the highest degree of stable mitochondria-ER encapsulations, coincident with fission-biased mitochondria and a high-flux respiratory state. Disruption of the mitochondria-ER contact protein PTPIP51 reduced lipid droplet clustering in the PPN state. Because cytomegalovirus is known to exploit host mitochondria remodeling, mitochondria-ER contacts, and metabolic output during infection, we tested whether this pre-existing host configuration is associated with cytomegalovirus permissiveness. PPN organoids exhibited greater murine cytomegalovirus infection and infectious output than matched monolayers or PBM. Together, these data define a resource of distinct protein characteristics between matched monolayer, spheroid, and organoid systems that should be considered for experimental design. We also uncover a mechanistic axis connecting 3D architecture, organelle contacts, metabolism, drug response, and viral permissiveness.

papers.title: A multi-scale forecasting framework to prioritize clinically-relevant antibiotic resistance alleles
papers.abstract: Established in vitro measures for the emergence of antimicrobial resistance, a critical global threat, can fail to predict which in vitro discovered mutations will dominate in the real world following widespread antibiotic use. Here, we introduce a multi-scale computational framework integrating genetic constraints and population pharmacokinetics and apply it to explain resistance allele success in Acinetobacter baumannii for the historic case of resistance to the fluoroquinolone antibiotic ciprofloxacin. By coupling intrinsic nucleotide substitution likelihoods with continuous-time stochastic modeling under fluctuating drug exposures, our framework clearly prioritizes the most common real world gyrA fluoroquinolone resistance allele S81L over rarer alleles, reflecting its clinical success. While gyrA serves as a proof-of-concept case study for direct, active-site drug-target interactions where the target space is constrained, we observe that the nucleotide substitution likelihoods are not explaining allele success in resistance-determining genes pmrB and adeS. Furthermore, "virtual twin" cohort simulations reveal that restricted drug penetration or compromised immunity expands selective windows, rescuing rare, low-fitness alleles. This advances our understanding of prospective, model-informed risk prediction during antibiotic development.

papers.title: Klebsiella taiwanensis sp. nov., and Pseudomonas ficus sp. nov., novel taxa isolated from figs (Ficus)
papers.abstract: Two bacterial strains, WOUb02T and WOUb67T, were isolated from fresh figs (Ficus spp.) collected from the island of Taiwan. Cells of WOUb02T and WOUb67T were Gram-stain-negative rods. Strain WOUb02T was non-motile, whereas WOUb67T exhibited motility. Physiologically, both strains grew optimally at 0.5% (w/v) NaCl and pH 8.0; WOUb02T grew optimally at 37{degrees}C, whereas WOUb67T grew optimally at 30{degrees}C. Based on 16S rRNA gene sequence similarity, the closest relatives to strains WOUb02T and WOUb67T were Klebsiella terrigena ATCC 33257T (98.2%) and Pseudomonas putida NBRC 14164T (99.9%) respectively. Subsequent phylogenetic analysis based on 16S rRNA gene sequences revealed that strains WOUb02T and WOUb67T formed distinct lineages within the genera Klebsiella and Pseudomonas, respectively. Further genomic analyses revealed that WOUb02T and WOUb67T shared average nucleotide identity and digital DNA-DNA hybridization values <95.0% and <70.0%, below the currently accepted thresholds for species-level delineation. Based on phenotypic and genotypic data, strains WOUb02T and WOUb67T could be distinguished from other species with validly published names and are considered to represent novel species in the genera Klebsiella and Pseudomonas, respectively, for which the names Klebsiella taiwanensis sp. nov., and Pseudomonas ficus sp. nov., are proposed. The type strains are WOUb02T (=NRRL-B 65719T =CCUG 77855T) and WOUb67T (=NRRL-B 65720T =CCUG 77856T).

papers.title: Effect of Moisture Content of Paddy (Phka Rumduol) on the Quality of White Rice (Oryza sativa L.)
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the impact of paddy moisture content on the quality parameters of white rice produced from Cambodia's premium fragrant variety, Phka Rumduol (Oryza sativa L.). A completely randomized design (CRD) was employed to evaluate the effect of moisture content on rice quality. Paddy samples were adjusted to four target moisture levels (10%, 12%, 14%, and 16%) and subsequently milled under controlled conditions. The CRD ensured unbiased allocation of samples across all treatments, minimizing experimental error during both moisture conditioning and milling processes. The results showed that moisture content had a significant effect (p < 0.05) on all measured quality parameters. Paddy at 14% moisture content produced the best results, with a head rice yield of 63.46 %, and a broken rice percentage of only 4.86 %. Grain appearance was also well preserved, with rice bran yield of 10.67 %, rice husk yield of 18.52 %, and yellow kernels averaging just 0.79 %. In contrast, moisture levels below 12% increased kernel brittleness, leading to breakage rates as high as 26.28 %, while levels above 16% caused grain deformation and discoloration. These findings highlight the importance of maintaining paddy moisture at 14% prior to milling to optimize recovery and preserve the high quality of Phka Rumduol rice. The study provides practical guidance for Cambodian rice processors aiming to improve product quality and strengthen competitiveness in international markets.

papers.title: Molecular dynamics simulations and in vivo binding studies indicate distinct membrane binding modes of plant lipid droplet proteins including binding via a hydrophobic face
papers.abstract: Plant lipid droplets (LDs) are specialized cellular subcompartments for lipid storage and key hubs for lipid metabolism. They have a unique structure: a hydrophobic core composed of neutral lipids enclosed by a phospholipid monolayer and associated proteins. Progress has been made in the identification and characterization of LD-associated plant proteins in recent years, raising the question of how these proteins bind to LDs. To investigate common structural features of LD association, we set up an in silico system using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to elucidate the nature of this interaction and to identify predicted binding regions of selected proteins. We then tested the importance of these regions for LD association by transient expression of truncated or mutated variants in tobacco pollen tubes. With this combined approach, we investigated the LD targeting region of thirteen LD-associated proteins. In several proteins, a distinct structural feature, a hydrophobic face, binds to LDs by interacting with the acyl chains of the phospholipid monolayer through large hydrophobic residues thereby pushing the headgroups to the sides. We also analyzed proteins previously assayed for LD association and demonstrate a correlation between predicted binding parameters and in vivo binding.

papers.title: Mitochondrial H2S and cytochrome c coordinate guard cell redox dynamics during stomatal immunity
papers.abstract: Stomatal pores modulate gas exchange between plants and the environment and are the first layer of defense against pathogens entry. Hydrogen sulfide (H2S) is a recognized component of the signalling network in guard cells that control stomatal responses. We previously showed that the mitochondrial H2S source {beta}-cyanoalanine synthase (CAS-C1) is required for flg22-induced stomatal closure. Using genetically encoded redox biosensors in Arabidopsis thaliana guard cells, we found that the mitochondrially-targeted H2S donor AP39 and the pathogen-associated molecular pattern (PAMP) flg22 both increased mitochondrial H2O2 within 5 min, while the flg22-triggered rise was attenuated in cas-c1 mutants. Dissipating the mitochondrial membrane potential ({Delta}{psi}m) with the uncoupler 2,4-dinitrophenol prevented both mitochondrial oxidation and stomatal closure. Cytochrome c (CYTc), the mobile electron carrier between complexes III and IV, proved essential for this pathway. CYTc-deficient lines showed a stomatal response similar than wild-type (wt) to ABA and light but failed to trigger stomatal closure upon exposure to different PAMPs. In these plants, neither AP39 nor flg22 induced guard cell mitochondrial hyperpolarization or an increase in cytosolic H2O2. By the dimedone-switch method, we show that CYTc is persulfidated in vivo, identifying this respiratory protein as a target of H2S-mediated posttranslational modification. At the whole-plant level, cytc plants were more susceptible to spray inoculation with Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato hrcC- at early stages of infection. Together, these results position CYTc as a mitochondrial node that links H2S signalling to guard cell redox dynamics during stomatal immunity.

papers.title: APOBEC3 Activation Drives Epitranscriptomic Remodeling and Clonal Hematopoiesis
papers.abstract: Stress and inflammatory cytokine-inducible APOBEC3 (A3) enzymes promote clonal evolution in many malignancies. We identified A3C overexpression in hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) following spaceflight-associated accelerated aging and in precancer myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs). However, the role of A3 in age-associated clonal hematopoiesis (CH) and precancer initiation remains unclear. To investigate the functional hierarchy among A3 enzymes, we performed lentiviral A3B, A3C, A3D, A3F, and A3G overexpression, whole genome, whole transcriptome and single-cell RNA sequencing analyses, and functional HSPC assays. While A3C and A3F induced more C-to-T DNA mutations; A3B, A3C, and A3G deregulated RNA splicing; and all A3 enzymes induced C-to-U RNA edits in HSPCs. In aged HSPCs, A3C overexpression enhanced replating and myeloid lineage skewing in humanized inflammatory niche mouse models typical of CH. Moreover, A3C-induced editing of CH-associated transcripts distinguished MPN from normal HSPCs. Thus, future strategies focused on APOBEC3C inhibition may prevent CH and precancer initiation.

papers.title: Compensatory Creatine Secretion Protects Against Drug-Induced Liver Injury via Desuccinylation
papers.abstract: ackground and aims: Effective therapeutic interventions for Drug induced liver injury (DILI) remain limited. N-myc downstream regulated gene-1 (NDRG1), a stress-responsive proteins, has an incompletely defined role in acetaminophen-induced liver injury. Method: Wild-type (WT), NDRG1Hep-flox, Hepatocyte-specific NDRG1 conditional knockout mice (NDRG1Hep-KO) were subjected to APAP-induced injury modeling. Liver and blood sample from patient were analyzed. Liver sample of mice subsequently underwent RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq), untargeted metabolomic profiling, single-cell sequencing, succinylation sequencing. For in vitro studies, AML-12 hepatocytes, RAW264.7 macrophages, and bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs), human Monocyte-Derived Macrophages, human hepatocyte organoids were utilized in experiments. Result: NDRG1 was upregulated in mouse and human DILI livers. NDRG1 conditional knockout significantly exacerbates DILI. Mechanistically, NDRG1 inhibited GAMT ubiquitination to enhance creatine production, and hepatocyte?derived creatine attenuated M1 polarization of liver macrophages by suppressing PHB1 succinylation at lysine 128. CXCL2? macrophages were identified as a major subpopulation regulated by NDRG1. Conclusion: Hepatocyte NDRG1 protects against APAP-DILI by driving GAMT-dependent creatine production and PHB1 K128 succinylation-dependent macrophage reprogramming.

papers.title: A specialized extracellular matrix patterns the conserved cortical protein EFA-6 at neuron-epidermal interfaces
papers.abstract: Sensory neurons establish intimate connections with the surrounding epidermis, where specialized extracellular matrix (ECM) help maintain neuron-epidermal interactions. However, whether and how this specialized ECM regulates the spatial organization of cortical proteins at these interfaces remains poorly understood. Here, we show a specialized ECM patterns the cortical microtubule regulator EFA-6 at neuron-epidermal interfaces in Caenorhabditis elegans. We show that EFA-6 in the epidermal cortex is enriched adjacent to the neurites of touch receptor neurons, characterized by discrete foci at the distal neurite and a diffuse distribution in the proximal neurite. We identify the specialized ECM components MEC-1 and HIM-4/hemicentin as regulators of EFA-6 spatial patterning at the interface between epidermis and neuronal processes. EFA-6 proteins contain an intrinsically disordered region (IDR) that is necessary and sufficient for EFA-6 targeting to and patterning at the neuron-epidermal interface. Within the IDR, we further identify an 8 residue motif that regulates enrichment and patterning of EFA-6 IDR at this interface. Finally, we find that EFA-6 contributes to age-dependent neurite defects in him-4 mutants. Together, our findings reveal how a specialized extracellular matrix and an intrinsically disordered region coordinate the spatial organization of a cortical MT regulator at neuron-epidermal interface.

papers.title: Transmural compression drives lymphatic endothelial dysfunction through Piezo1-CaMKII signaling
papers.abstract: Background: Secondary lymphedema is characterized by progressive lymphatic dysfunction, chronic inflammation, and tissue fibrosis, but how mechanical changes during disease progression contribute to lymphatic failure remains poorly understood. Lymphatic vessels initially undergo intraluminal pressure-induced dilation, whereas advanced disease is associated with extraluminal compression resulting from tissue remodeling. We investigated how these different mechanical stimuli affect lymphatic endothelial function. Methods and Results: We developed a human lymphatic vessel-on-chip model enabling independent control of intra- and extraluminal pressure. In contrast to vessel dilation, extraluminal compression profoundly disrupted lymphatic endothelial barrier integrity, increasing permeability and causing junctional disorganization, while also inducing a strong pro-inflammatory transcriptional response. Mechanistically, compression induced sustained intracellular Ca2 influx and activated the mechanosensitive ion channel Piezo1. Piezo1 inhibition attenuated compression-induced Ca2 responses and protected endothelial barrier integrity, identifying Piezo1 as an upstream mediator of compression-induced dysfunction. Downstream, compression-induced Ca2 signaling activated Ca2 /calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII), whose inhibition preserved endothelial junctional integrity and reduced both barrier dysfunction and inflammatory activation. In a murine model of secondary lymphedema, CaMKII inhibition improved lymphatic function and reduced lymphedema-associated tissue remodeling. Conclusions: These findings identify a Piezo1-CaMKII signaling axis that links pathological extraluminal compression to lymphatic endothelial dysfunction and inflammation. Targeting this pathway may help preserve lymphatic function during lymphedema progression.

papers.title: Oral microbiome and DNA virome profiling in pigs reveals age-associated dynamics and extracellular recovery of Streptococcus suis-associated phage lineages
papers.abstract: The pig oral cavity is a critical interface for microbial transmission and herd health monitoring, yet its microbiome and virome remains poorly characterised. We performed shotgun metagenomic sequencing of oral fluids from pigs across 15 commercial farms in Ireland, using paired bulk and virus-like particles (VLP) enrichment to capture comprehensive microbial and DNA virome diversity. Microbial communities shifted progressively with age, with early post-weaning animals enriched in environmental genera such as Pseudomonas and Staphylococcus and later stages dominated by lactic acid bacteria and anaerobes. Only 20.6% of vOTUs could be assigned to a known genus, with the most abundant being Astrithrvirus, which increased with age. Both microbiome and DNA virome exhibited predictable, coordinated age-associated succession with strong cross-domain coupling supported by virus-host networks. Functional profiling of the microbiome revealed that predicted carbohydrate substrates tracked the dietary transitions, while accessory viral functions partitioned by lifestyle and host. The early post-weaning stage was characterised by high abundance of viral integration and excision functions, as well as elevated resistome diversity that was almost exclusively of prokaryotic origin rather than viral. Importantly, 26 of the 25,223 vOTUs identified were predicted to target Streptococcus suis, providing the first metagenomic catalogue of such phages from pig oral environments. These findings expand our understanding of oral microbiome-virome dynamics and establish a framework for integrated microbiome and viromics approaches that could enable therapeutic phage discovery and inform microbiome-targeted interventions in pig production systems.

papers.title: Adjuvant myeloperoxidase inhibition promotes B and T cell mediated control of murine melanoma metastasis
papers.abstract: Metastasis is the spread of cancer cells from primary tumors to distant organs and accounts for the majority of melanoma deaths, with a 5-year survival rate of only 30%. Despite strong evidence that myeloid cells promote metastasis, there are limited clinically effective myeloid-directed therapies. Here, we demonstrate that targeting myeloperoxidase (MPO), a myeloid-lineage restricted enzyme, significantly reduced multi-organ metastatic burden using an immunocompetent mouse model of spontaneous melanoma. Adjuvant MPO inhibition remodeled the metastatic microenvironment by a reduction in Ly6G+Ly6C+ myeloid cells and enrichment of B and T cell populations. Importantly, adjuvant MPO inhibitor-mediated metastatic control was dependent upon B, CD8+ T cells and CD4+ T cells, and rapidly reduced circulating and disseminated tumor cells. MPO inhibition markedly decreased NET release, while NET deficiency and inhibition recapitulated the anti-metastatic effects of targeting MPO, implicating NETs as a potential downstream mediator of MPO-driven metastasis. We further validated these findings in a distinct spontaneous breast cancer model where adjuvant MPO inhibition similarly reduced multi-organ metastatic burden with comparable changes within the metastatic immune microenvironment. Collectively, our studies introduce MPO as a druggable regulator of metastasis where MPO inhibition limits metastatic disease by targeting immunosuppressive myeloid cells.

papers.title: Joint Estimation of Mother and Daughter Protein Regulatory Networks Quantifies Inheritance in Yeast Lineages
papers.abstract: Live-cell imaging tracks multiple protein levels within individual cells across divisions in real time, enabling direct measurement of how regulatory dynamics are inherited by a daughter cell from her mother. This technology presents a unique opportunity to directly observe longitudinal dynamics, in contrast to single-cell RNA sequencing, which can only measure cells cross-sectionally. However, there is a lack of computational methods for analyzing live-cell imaging data. Existing frameworks based on ordinary differential equations (ODEs) estimate networks from individual time series, but adapting them to mother-daughter pairs poses a dilemma: pooling both cells forces complete inheritance, while fitting each cell separately starves the short daughter trajectory of timepoints needed for reliable estimation. To address this gap, we develop PRNODE (Protein Regulatory Networks via ODEs), which models each cell's network as a deviation from a shared regulatory scaffold and estimates the scaffold and both deviations jointly under a fused group-lasso penalty. The mother's longer time series thereby supports the daughter's estimate, while allowing the two networks to differ wherever the data demand it. We then propose a novel measure of inheritance based on comparing the rate of change of protein levels between the mother's and daughter's networks. Across simulation studies, we find that PRNODE outperforms existing ODE estimation methods in recovering the networks of daughter cells and in estimating inheritance. Finally, we apply PRNODE to many mother-daughter pairs of Saccharomyces cerevisiae observed over a 9-hour period at 12-minute intervals. Many estimated networks show a negative feedback loop between the cell-cycle inhibitor Whi5 and the cyclin Clb2, which together sustain cell-cycle oscillations. We also find that the measured inheritance tracks the number of regulatory edges a daughter shares with her mother with the same sign, more than the presence of any single edge. PRNODE is available as an R package at https://github.com/shirmath/LIC_methods.

papers.title: Agreement between structure prediction tools does not indicate biological plausibility in cancer fusion proteins
papers.abstract: While protein-folding software has made great strides in recent years, reliability is known to be poorer on novel structures and failure modes are not fully characterised. Cancer fusion proteins present a unique case of proteins absent from model training data but constructed from parents with known structures. This study tests four popular protein-folding tools on three categories of protein: control, cancer-associated, and uncharacterised fusion proteins. We assessed computational performance, accuracy, and distinct failure modes. For well-characterised proteins, all tools tested returned the correct structures in all but one case, with some tools returning an average of two distinct structural forms in the exception. For characterised cancer-associated proteins, most predictions were highly accurate; poorer predictions often still returned some consistent high-confidence domains but produced divergent results in other areas that were both variable between tools and at odds with experimental structures. For cancer fusion proteins having available parent-protein reference structures, results fell into two clear categories. Roughly half contained structures matching to the functional domains of their parent proteins at high confidence, in keeping with biological expectation for these proteins; the others contained little evidence of matching structures, independent of the tool used. Predictions for fusion proteins differed far more between tools than those for characterised proteins with a median inter-tool TM-score 0.272 versus 0.853 respectively. However, agreement between tools did not indicate a more biologically plausible prediction. For example, all tools predicted drastically different structures for fusion protein TMPRSS2-ERG, but all predictions still contained the core ERG functional domains; conversely, all tools produced highly consistent structures for DNAJB1-PRKACA, but none of the predictions contained the expected functional regions. We recommend that users of these tools use care and caution in the assessments of outputs and consider biological knowledge before blindly trusting results.

papers.title: ViruDB: An Assay-Aware Molecular Database and Endpoint-Adaptive Multimodal Learning Framework for Antibiofilm, Quorum-Sensing Inhibition, and Antivirulence Research
papers.abstract: Antibiofilm and quorum-sensing inhibitory molecules have become increasingly attractive candidates to complement traditional antibacterial approaches, but the experimental evidence ranges from heterogeneous assays, organisms, methods of activity measurement, and chemical representation. We created ViruDB, a molecular evidence resource that is assay-aware, and tested an endpoint-adaptive multimodal learning framework for quantitative activity prediction. Curated collection of 8765 experimental evidence records for 3563 unique molecules: 2,959 quantitative observations, of which 2,345 were antibiofilm, 569 were quorum-sensing inhibition [QSI], and 45 were antivirulence. Molecular representations included 217 2D descriptors from RDKit, 2,048-bit ECFP4 fingerprints, molecular graphs, and some information about the biological context. A molecule- and scaffold-disjoint primary partition was used, which resulted in 2,339 observations in the training set, 265 observations in the validation set and 355 observations in the independent test set. ViruFusion-TaskExpert-MTL and an endpoint specific combination with classical regressors were selected by validation. The final predictor yielded an RMSE value of 0.5460 and an R2 of 0.4816 on the antibiofilm activity dataset (n=286) and an RMSE value of 0.5744 and an R2 of 0.4082 on the QSI dataset (n=67) in the reported frozen independent evaluation. Exploratory anti-virulence regression (n=2 test observations). The results validate quantitative, endpoint based prioritization under chemical novelty and highlight the significance of assay provenance, assay leakage control and external biological assay validation.

papers.title: Modeling Host-Virus Interactions of Avian Corona Virus Reveals Cytokine Feedback as a driver of Strain-Specific Immune Response
papers.abstract: The interplay between RNA viral dynamics and innate immunity remains poorly understood, mainly because RNA viruses trigger highly nonlinear cytokine responses. We address this using infectious bronchitis virus (IBV), a major poultry pathogen, as a model system. We developed a set of mathematical models and compared those with experimental data from two IBV strains infecting chicken macrophages.By model fitting and supervised Machine Learning we reveal that positive feedback in interferon- production is essential to reproduce the dynamics of one IBV strain but likely absent in the other. We further provide strain-specific estimations of key parameters such as infection rates, production and decay rates of virus and cytokine levels. Notably, different strains produced distinctive cytokine profiles, highlighting feedback as a key determinant of strain-specific immune signatures. Our results establish a quantitative framework for dissecting host-virus interactions and uncover cytokine feedback as a generic yet underappreciated feature in models of RNA virus kinetics.

papers.title: EXPA delivery links cell polarity to polarized growth in root hair
papers.abstract: Turgor pressure, which drives irreversible cell wall enlargement and thereby cell growth, is isotropic. Polarized plant cell growth therefore requires spatially regulated wall-loosening to confine growth to specific domains. These domains are often marked by localized ROP GTPase activity, but how this polarity is translated into localized wall loosening remains unclear. Here, we investigated the delivery of EXPA7, a trichoblast-specific -expansin that facilitates wall loosening and enlargement during root hair growth. We show that ROP activation directs EXPA7 recruitment to the root hair initiation domain through brefeldin-A-sensitive vesicular trafficking, with YIP4a/b required for its normal secretion and wall-deposition. The recruited EXPA7 contributes to ROP2-induced wall enlargement, and its accumulation accompanies local cell wall bulging. Our findings provide a mechanistic link between ROP activation and cell growth, suggesting how signals converging on ROP activation may control growth.

papers.title: Female sex determination in zebrafish does not depend on M ribosomal RNA transcription
papers.abstract: Ribosome biogenesis is an essential process in all cells across organisms, especially during development of the gonad. How ribosome biogenesis impacts gonad development remains to be understood. Work in zebrafish has identified distinct oocyte- and somatic cell-type ribosomal DNA (rDNA) loci, M rDNA and S rDNA, respectively, and it has been hypothesized that the M rDNA locus or the M ribosomal RNA (rRNA)-containing ribosome could function as the major female sex determinant. To better understand how the M and S rDNA loci are regulated during zebrafish gonadogenesis, we visualized M and S rRNA transcripts in vivo in developing bipotential gonads, ovaries, and testes. We find that oogonia and early spermatogonia contain M and S rRNA transcripts, while germ cells of the biopotential gonad contain M rRNA transcripts almost exclusively. We find that M rRNA transcription is preferentially maintained in differentiating prophase I oocytes. In contrast, M rRNA transcripts are not present in late spermatogonia, which instead exhibit exclusive S rRNA transcription prior to further differentiation where S rRNA transcription becomes progressively absent. We determine that M rRNA transcription initiation precedes and does not depend on the onset of meiosis. rRNA visualization in a female sex differentiation and ribosome biogenesis mutant, rbpms2, showed that ectopic S rRNA transcription may be disruptive to continued oogenesis, but this is not regulated by the DNA methyltransferases, Dnmt3bb.1, Dnmt3bb.2, and Dnmt3bb.3. Altogether, we find that transcription of M rRNA does not function as a female sex determinant in zebrafish gonadogenesis, though its preferential maintenance in oocytes may be essential to ribosome biogenesis, meiotic entry and progression, and female sex differentiation.

papers.title: Interaction of yeast Vps13 with the calcium binding proteins Cdc31 and calmodulin
papers.abstract: Vps13 is a member of the bridge-like lipid transfer protein superfamily involved in transport of lipids between different intracellular membranes. In yeast, deletion of VPS13 exhibits several distinct phenotypes due to preventing interorganelle lipid transfer between many different organelles. Vps13 shuttles lipids through a long hydrophobic channel, but how this activity is regulated in the cell is not yet understood. Studies in yeast and human cells have implicated small calcium-binding proteins, Cdc31 in yeast and calmodulin in mammalian cells, as potential regulators of Vps13 activity. This report identifies the binding site on Vps13 for Cdc31, the yeast ortholog of centrin. The yeast calmodulin protein Cmd1 binds Vps13 through the same site and separate Cmd1-Vps13 and Cdc31-Vps13 complexes co-exist in vivo. Association of Cmd1 with Vps13, but not Cdc31, is sensitive to the presence of Ca2+. A mutant of VPS13 that is unable to interact with either Cdc31 or Cmd1 is specifically defective in mitochondrial homeostasis and endoplasmic-reticulum (ER)-phagy, indicating that Vps13 binding to Cdc31 and/or Cmd1 is important for a subset of VPS13 functions.

papers.title: Structural basis for assembly of human cN1A filaments
papers.abstract: Human cytosolic 5'-nucleotidase 1A (cN1A), which catalyzes the hydrolysis of AMP to adenosine, is a prominent autoantigen in the progressive myopathy inclusion body myositis (IBM). Detection of anti-cN1A autoantibodies is a supportive criterion for IBM diagnosis, and mice immunized actively or passively with cN1A develop an IBM phenotype. However, how cN1A breaks immunotolerance is not yet known. Despite its clinical significance, the subcellular localization of cN1A is not well understood, and its structure has not been determined. Here, we show that human cN1A is most highly expressed in type 2 myofibers and tends to localize near the periphery of muscle fibers, but is either weakly expressed or undetectable in commonly used human cell lines. Ectopic expression of cN1A in such cells resulted in spontaneous assembly of cN1A into filamentous structures strikingly similar to metabolic filaments formed by the nucleotide biosynthesis enzymes IMP dehydrogenase (IMPDH) and CTP synthase (CTPS). However, cN1A filaments did not co-localize with IMPDH or CTPS filaments and were not responsive to compounds that induce IMPDH and CTPS assembly. Negative stain electron microscopy (EM) showed that purified recombinant cN1A protein spontaneously polymerizes, suggesting filament assembly in cells is driven by intrinsic properties of cN1A. We then determined the structure of the cN1A filament by cryo-EM, which revealed that cN1A monomers assemble end-on-end into a polar helical filament and allowed us to identify contacts mediating filament assembly. Structure-guided mutations designed to abolish filament assembly prevented cN1A filament formation in cells, establishing the structural basis for cN1A filament assembly.

papers.title: Integrative structural biology of a giant marine virus reveals architectural and functional complexity beyond icosahedral symmetry
papers.abstract: Knowledge of giant virus diversity has expanded rapidly; however, isolated representatives remain scarce, and few have been examined at high resolution. Here, we characterized haptophyte-infecting Prymnesium kappa virus RF02 (PkV-RF02) using integrative structural biology. The ~3 [A] resolution structure obtained by block-based cryo-electron microscopy reconstruction shows a pseudoT=219 icosahedral shell built from over 20 different proteins and approximately 10,000 polypeptides, a multi-layered stabilization network reinforced by 20,000 disulphide bridges, two penton variants evenly distributed in the capsid, and a protein channel crossing the internal membrane. Cross-linking mass spectrometry defines the intricate capsid-membrane-core interaction network, which includes a second major capsid protein, a third penton variant, and multiple biochemical functions packaged within the virion. Phospho- and glycoproteomics reveal widespread post-translational modifications, with approximately 50% of proteins phosphorylated and uncommon methyl-N-acetylated viosamine glycans. This study provides a comprehensive structural and interaction map that highlights organizational and functional innovations underlying giant virus assembly.

papers.title: Model evaluation metrics of Virtual Cell Challenge 2026
papers.abstract: Virtual cell models aim to predict the effects of genetic, environmental, chemical and other perturbations in silico, reducing the dependency on complex and costly experiments. The Virtual Cell Challenge 2026 motivates the field toward this goal, tasking models with zero-shot prediction of the transcriptional responses to CRISPRi knockdowns in six human cell lines. The faithfulness of a model to the experiment is assessed by metrics that compare its predictions with the real data, and designing such metrics is not trivial. We developed the metrics of the 2026 Challenge around three principles: a metric should (i) reflect the biological information extracted from experiments, (ii) be calibrated on a repeat of the experiment, and (iii) resist shortcut solutions that raise the score without predicting the response. Here we present the six resulting metrics, the reasoning behind each of them, and their evaluations on the Challenge data. Two of the metrics compare the pseudobulk expression profiles of predicted and measured cells, while four assess the genes that respond to each perturbation, the central readout of a Perturb-seq experiment. The metrics are implemented in cell-eval2, an open-source Python package. On the Challenge data, all six metrics score a repeat of the experiment above the mean baseline, and the shortcut solutions that the metrics of the 2025 Challenge left open can no longer raise the score. The new metrics are therefore more robust than the previous ones.

papers.title: NADH regulation shapes competing acetate flux responses in Escherichia coli: kinetic modelling of the tricarboxylic acid cycle and acetate production
papers.abstract: Overflow metabolism occurs when cells divert carbon towards fermentative products despite oxygen availability. In rapidly growing Escherichia coli, it is primarily characterised by acetate secretion. An elevated NADH/NAD+ ratio has been proposed to contribute to this behaviour, but the mechanisms linking redox imbalance to acetate production remain unclear. We developed a kinetic model linking pyruvate metabolism, the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, and acetate formation to examine how cofactor availability and NADH-mediated enzyme regulation influence carbon partitioning. The model combines thermodynamically consistent reversible rate laws with NADH inhibition of pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) and citrate synthase, and was calibrated using Bayesian inference to account for parameter uncertainty. We examined steady-state responses to changes in the target NADH/NAD+ ratio and the total NAD(H) pool size. With both inhibitory interactions included, lowering the target redox ratio increased acetate-producing flux, contrary to the experimentally observed reduction in acetate secretion. Substantially attenuating the effective NADH response of PDH recovered the experimental direction of this response. Additionally, to reproduce the observed reduction in acetate secretion following NAD(H)-pool expansion, a weak but non-zero PDH response was required. These findings suggest that cofactor-dependent kinetics and NADH-mediated regulation can jointly contribute to carbon redistribution between the TCA cycle and acetate production. Within this restricted model, whether a more reduced redox state promotes acetate-producing flux depends critically on the effective NADH sensitivity of PDH.

papers.title: Targeting MondoA Sensitizes B-ALL Cells to Asparaginase and Reveals Glutathione-Associated Protection
papers.abstract: Background: L-Asparaginase (ASNase) is central to acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) therapy, but resistance and long-term cytotoxic effects remain challenging. We investigated whether MondoA (MLXIP) modulates ASNase sensitivity. Methods: Viability and apoptosis were assessed in CRISPR-Cas9-generated MondoA-knockout (MKO), MondoA-overexpressing (MOE), and Cas9-only control (WT) Nalm6 B-ALL cells following ASNase exposure or glutamine depletion. Omics, ChIP-seq, and patient-RNA-seq examined MondoA-ASNS associations. Results: MondoA deficiency was associated with reduced ASNS mRNA and protein abundance. MYC binding to the ASNS promoter was reduced in MKO cells, suggesting an indirect transcriptional link. MondoA and ASNS expression correlated in patient samples, particularly in T-ALL (r = 0.769). MKO cells showed increased ASNase, but not doxorubicin or vincristine, sensitivity. Glutamine withdrawal during ASNase treatment further reduced viability. GSH-associated protection was strongest in biallelic MKO2. Conclusion: MondoA status was associated with ASNS abundance and ASNase response, warranting further investigation of these processes as candidate determinants of ASNase sensitivity.

papers.title: Caspase-7 cleavage repurposes AAK1 to suppress mRNA decay and promote tolerance to anti-tubulin agents
papers.abstract: Prolonged mitotic arrest imposed by anti-tubulin chemotherapy suppresses transcription, making mRNA preservation critical for tumor-cell survival. Here, we identify an unexpected kinase-repurposing mechanism that sustains this adaptation. A kinome-wide screen revealed clathrin-adaptor kinase AAK1 as a determinant of taxane tolerance. During mitotic arrest, CDK1 phosphorylates AAK1 at T389 to enhance catalytic activity, while caspase-7 cleaves AAK1 at D767, removing a clathrin-binding domain. These modifications produce a cleaved fragment with reduced clathrin association and increased association with CCR4-NOT, suppressing mRNA decay and maintaining glycolytic gene expression. Mutant-rescues establish that both phosphorylation and cleavage contribute to cancer-cell survival during paclitaxel-induced arrest. A clinical-stage AAK1 inhibitor developed for neuropathic pain sensitized cancer cells to paclitaxel. Together, these findings reveal how coordinated phosphorylation and proteolysis repurpose a trafficking kinase to maintain mRNA stability, uncovering an unexpected tolerance-promoting function of caspase cleavage and a therapeutically actionable vulnerability of chemotherapy-arrested cancer cells.

papers.title: TMEM2 Deficiency Causes Cleft Palate and Disrupts Vascular Development
papers.abstract: Hyaluronan (HA) is a major component of the extracellular matrix during craniofacial development. Studies of hyaluronan synthase 2 (HAS2) have established that HA synthesis is required for normal palatal development. However, the contribution of HA degradation to this process remains poorly understood. TMEM2 is a cell-surface hyaluronidase, and previous studies have demonstrated its role in neural crest cell (NCC) migration and the survival of post-migratory NCCs. Previous Wnt1-Cre-mediated deletion of Tmem2 caused early embryonic lethality, preventing assessment of later palatal development. Here, we used Sox10-Cre to delete Tmem2 in the NCC lineage and investigate its role in palatogenesis. Conditional knockout (CKO) embryos developed complete cleft palate. Palatal shelves elevated but remained smaller than controls, with reduced proliferation and increased apoptosis. ZsGreen lineage labeling revealed reduced directional organization of NCC-derived cells, accompanied by widespread HA accumulation throughout the palatal mesenchyme. To identify molecular changes accompanying these abnormalities, we performed RNA sequencing, which revealed enrichment of hypoxia-related transcriptional programs and suppression of cell-cycle programs. Increased HIF-1? and pimonidazole labeling provided complementary evidence of tissue hypoxia. Vascular analyses revealed altered CD31-positive vessel architecture, reduced contact between NCC-derived cells and vessels, and fewer PDGFR?-positive cells. Together, these findings identify TMEM2-dependent HA remodeling as an important component of palatal development and link its disruption to altered NCC-derived mesenchymal organization, vascular and perivascular abnormalities, and tissue hypoxia.

papers.title: Infant formula composition is linked to distinct patterns of early gut colonization
papers.abstract: Early-life nutrition shapes the gut microbiota and can have long-term health implications. While infant formula feeding is widespread, it remains unclear how variations in its nutritional components shape microbiome colonization. Here, we reconstructed 62 components across the 17 infant formulas consumed during the first three months of life in 240 exclusively formula-fed infants in the Lifelines-NEXT birth cohort. Formula composition varied widely and several micronutrients, including vitamin E and iodine, were associated with species richness. Components were also associated with species-level colonization patterns. Higher iron content was associated with reduced Bifidobacterium breve and Bifidobacterium bifidum and increased Clostridium paraputrificum. Follow-up in vitro growth assays on infant-derived stool isolates showed that Bifidobacterium breve and Bifidobacterium bifidum tolerated iron limitation, while C. paraputrificum did not, consistent with the association signals. These findings show that infant formulas are not all alike and differences in component concentration affect microbiome colonization in early-life.

papers.title: DRP1 Orchestrates RNA Virus Permissiveness Through Metabolic Reprogramming Independent of Mitochondrial Dynamics
papers.abstract: Viruses reprogram host metabolism and mitochondrial dynamics to support replication, yet how these processes govern viral permissiveness remains unclear. Using SARS-CoV-2 alongside other RNA viruses JEV, VSV, and HCV, we identify DRP1 as a central determinant of the virus-permissive cellular state beyond mitochondrial fission. While RNA viruses induce pronounced mitochondrial fragmentation linked to enhanced permissiveness, MFN1 conferred potent antiviral protection independent of type I interferon. Targeting DRP1-associated functions pharmacologically suppresses viral replication, accompanied by decreased glycolysis and enhanced oxidative metabolism. Remarkably, genetic depletion of DRP1 itself potently restricts viral replication in both wild-type and MFN1-deficient cells despite persistent mitochondrial fragmentation in the latter, demonstrating that MFN1 and mitochondrial elongation are dispensable for antiviral restriction. Together, these findings identify DRP1 as a key regulator of viral permissiveness operating beyond mitochondrial morphology. By uncoupling mitochondrial morphology from antiviral regulation, our study highlights DRP1-associated pathways as promising targets for host-directed antiviral strategies.

papers.title: CDK1 and MAPK/Erk prime maternal proteins for Calcineurin-dependent dephosphorylation during the oocyte-to-embryo transition in Drosophila
papers.abstract: The transition from oocyte to embryo relies on the utilization of maternal macromolecules that accumulate during oogenesis. Change in phosphorylation status of maternal proteins is thought to drive developmental events during egg activation (EA) given that transcription does not occur during this time. To determine how mature oocytes acquire phosphorylation signatures on maternal proteins that are compatible with phospho-changes at EA, we analyzed phosphorylation dynamics during oocyte maturation (OM). We found widespread acquisition of phosphorylation at CDK1-MAPK sites during OM, and these sites were largely dephosphorylated during EA. We determined that the calcium-stimulated phosphatase Calcineurin is required for dephosphorylation of CDK1-MAPK substrates at EA; genetic perturbation of CDK1 or Calcineurin altered phosphorylation patterns at EA and induced precocious embryonic translation in oocytes. Ex vivo developmental assays revealed crosstalk between MAPK and CDK1 during OM: while depletion of either MAPK or CDK1 alone mildly impacts gross oocyte morphogenesis during OM, reducing the activity of both together dramatically reduced OM efficiency. Further, in MAPK-depleted conditions, CDK1 activity levels drastically increase in a temporally-sensitive manner, suggesting compensation for MAPK by CDK1 to ensure faithful establishment of maternal phospho-protein load. Finally, we show that the receipt of sperm during fertilization has no impact on phosphorylation events at EA. Our analyses connect the earliest events in embryonic initiation to the factors that keep oocytes arrested, providing novel insights as to the dynamics and mechanisms of maternal phospho-protein regulation during the transition from oogenesis to embryogenesis.
